entries.name: Introduction
entries.description: Nitro is a full-stack server framework, compatible with any runtime and any deployment target.

entries.name: Quick Start
entries.description: Start with a fresh Nitro project or adopt it in your current Vite project.

entries.name: Nitro Renderer
entries.description: Use a renderer to handle all unmatched routes with custom HTML or a templating system.

entries.name: Routing
entries.description: Nitro supports filesystem routing to automatically map files to routes. By combining code-splitting with compiled routes, it removes the need for a runtime router, leaving only minimal compiled logic.

entries.name: Nitro Server Entry
entries.description: Use a server entry to create a global middleware that runs for all routes before they are matched.

entries.name: Cache
entries.description: Nitro provides a caching system built on top of the storage layer, powered by ocache.

entries.name: KV Storage
entries.description: Nitro provides a built-in storage layer that can abstract filesystem or database or any other data source.

entries.name: Configuration
entries.description: Customize and extend Nitro defaults.

entries.name: Database
entries.description: Nitro provides a built-in and lightweight SQL database layer.

entries.name: Lifecycle
entries.description: Understand how Nitro runs and serves incoming requests to your application.

entries.name: OpenAPI
entries.description: Nitro can automatically generate an OpenAPI specification from your route handlers and serve interactive API documentation.

entries.name: Plugins
entries.description: Use plugins to extend Nitro's runtime behavior.

entries.name: Tasks
entries.description: Nitro tasks allow on-off operations in runtime.

entries.name: WebSocket
entries.description: Nitro provides cross-platform WebSocket support powered by CrossWS and H3.

entries.name: Nightly Channel
entries.description: Nitro has a nightly release channel that automatically releases for every commit to main branch to try latest changes.
